The insurance start rule uses the 'first working day'. If the contract starts on the 1st but the first actual working day is later (weekend or holiday, e.g. contract from Sat 01.06, first day Mon 03.06), the rule gives 01.07 instead of 01.06. Should the rule use the contractual start date or the actual first working day?

New hires often move to Switzerland when they start, or move away from it. Is the home address the current one or the one that applies from the first working day? The country decides source-tax liability, the canton and all the cross-border questions, so the answer changes which questions are asked.

In step 6 the Liechtenstein cross-border questions come after denomination, spouse employment and all the children questions. A Liechtenstein resident who returns daily (or expects at most 45 non-return days) gets 'in principle no source tax liability' and no tariff code, so their denomination, spouse-employment and children answers are not needed by any party (G-01). Should the Liechtenstein questions come first so those questions are skipped? Or, if the order stays, should those answers be discarded on submission like other answers that no longer apply? Or does HR need them anyway in case the case changes later?

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the calculator returns the normal tariff plus 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement), per F-zh_source_tax_calculator-cc19c7. AC-08.4.3 records only 'the normal tariff code'. Should this reservation also be recorded and flagged for HR in that case?

AC-02.2.2 keeps the house number required even though the spec says no source confirms that every address has one. An employee whose address has no house number (rural address, named building, etc.) could not submit at all. Should the house number be required, optional, or allow an explicit 'no house number'?

"Feeds the civil status entered at the fund (pension_fund_civil_status) and, for employees subject to source tax, the calculator's civil status group (calculator_civil_status)." - Internal snake_case rule ids are written into the business description of the Civil status item instead of business terms.

"(The expression shows the contribution of one child; for several children the contributions are added up.)" - This refers to an internal formula/expression representation of the rule, not business language.
"(rule subject_to_source_tax, owned by the source tax section)" - A code-style rule identifier appears in acceptance-criterion prose.
"(per-child result, rule child_result)" - A code-style rule identifier appears in acceptance-criterion prose.
"(rule cross_border_tariff: daily return with a certificate of residence handed in" - A code-style rule identifier appears in acceptance-criterion prose.

"(rule subject_to_source_tax: country of residence and, for residents of Switzerland, Swiss citizenship, C permit, civil status and spouse details)" - A code-style rule identifier appears in acceptance-criterion prose.
"compare all inferred rows of child_result and the cross-border paths" - An internal rule identifier is used instead of the business term 'per-child result'.

info.message: Before submission, can the employee save partway and come back later, and is there a review/summary of all answers before the final submit? After submission, does the employee get a confirmation? Submission is final (read-only), so these decide what the employee can check before locking it.

Are there business limits on the first working day, e.g. it must not be in the past or more than N months ahead? Is there a plausibility check on the employee's and spouse's dates of birth (minimum working age)? The pension fund only requires the DD.MM.YYYY format.

AC-03.1.2 ('the question makes clear the date must be the currently agreed one') cannot be tested as written. Is there agreed wording for the question, or a business requirement such as showing the date HR has on file?

Nationality (and the country of the home address and of the spouse's residence) is 'a country by English name'. Which list of countries/nationalities should be offered, and how do stateless employees or employees with unclear status answer the nationality question? Only 'Switzerland vs not' matters for the rule.

The example tables mix 'required' and 'asked' as expected results for questions the text says must be answered. Examples: spouse nationality 'required' for Tomás vs 'asked' for the registered partner; spouse residence 'required' vs 'asked'; in US-05.1, C permit 'required' for Maria vs 'asked' for Tomás. Is there a real difference (i.e. may some of these be left empty), or are they the same?

The spouse's country of residence matters only as 'lives in Switzerland or not'. Under data minimisation (G-01), should we ask the full country, or only 'Does your spouse/partner live in Switzerland? yes/no'?

'Minor' vs 'Adult in first education': on which date is the child's age judged? The submission date, the first working day, or the start of the tax year? A child who turns 18 around the start date would otherwise be classified differently.

The permit reminder is 'worded by HR', but no text is given. Who provides the final wording and when (before build or configurable later)? Is it shown only at the end, or also elsewhere (e.g. in a confirmation)?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: What does Pensionskasse Muster expect in its required 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or canton of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The fund's list has only the 26 Swiss cantons and the field is required; employees abroad (e.g. Konstanz, Liechtenstein) cannot be registered without an answer. Provisionally the canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland.
options: Canton of work (e.g. Zurich) for everyone, entered by HR
Canton of residence; the fund has another way for employees abroad
open_questions.recommendation: Keep D-002 (ask residents only); a domain expert verifies with Pensionskasse Muster.

open_questions.recommendation: Keep D-003 provisional mapping; domain expert verifies with the fund.

open_questions.question: Is HR's final source tax liability rule complete, and does 'lives here' mean lives in Switzerland?

open_questions.recommendation: Confirm the decision table of subject_to_source_tax with HR.

questions.question: The insurance start rule uses the 'first working day'. If the contract starts on the 1st but the first actual working day is later (weekend or holiday, e.g. contract from Sat 01.06, first day Mon 03.06), the rule gives 01.07 instead of 01.06. Should the rule use the contractual start date or the actual first working day?

New hires often move to Switzerland when they start, or move away from it. Is the home address the current one or the one that applies from the first working day? The country decides source-tax liability, the canton and all the cross-border questions, so the answer changes which questions are asked.

In step 6 the Liechtenstein cross-border questions come after denomination, spouse employment and all the children questions. A Liechtenstein resident who returns daily (or expects at most 45 non-return days) gets 'in principle no source tax liability' and no tariff code, so their denomination, spouse-employment and children answers are not needed by any party (G-01). Should the Liechtenstein questions come first so those questions are skipped? Or, if the order stays, should those answers be discarded on submission like other answers that no longer apply? Or does HR need them anyway in case the case changes later?

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the calculator returns the normal tariff plus 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement), per F-zh_source_tax_calculator-cc19c7. AC-08.4.3 records only 'the normal tariff code'. Should this reservation also be recorded and flagged for HR in that case?

AC-02.2.2 keeps the house number required even though the spec says no source confirms that every address has one. An employee whose address has no house number (rural address, named building, etc.) could not submit at all. Should the house number be required, optional, or allow an explicit 'no house number'?

Before submission, can the employee save partway and come back later, and is there a review/summary of all answers before the final submit? After submission, does the employee get a confirmation? Submission is final (read-only), so these decide what the employee can check before locking it.

Are there business limits on the first working day, e.g. it must not be in the past or more than N months ahead? Is there a plausibility check on the employee's and spouse's dates of birth (minimum working age)? The pension fund only requires the DD.MM.YYYY format.

AC-03.1.2 ('the question makes clear the date must be the currently agreed one') cannot be tested as written. Is there agreed wording for the question, or a business requirement such as showing the date HR has on file?

Nationality (and the country of the home address and of the spouse's residence) is 'a country by English name'. Which list of countries/nationalities should be offered, and how do stateless employees or employees with unclear status answer the nationality question? Only 'Switzerland vs not' matters for the rule.

The example tables mix 'required' and 'asked' as expected results for questions the text says must be answered. Examples: spouse nationality 'required' for Tomás vs 'asked' for the registered partner; spouse residence 'required' vs 'asked'; in US-05.1, C permit 'required' for Maria vs 'asked' for Tomás. Is there a real difference (i.e. may some of these be left empty), or are they the same?

The spouse's country of residence matters only as 'lives in Switzerland or not'. Under data minimisation (G-01), should we ask the full country, or only 'Does your spouse/partner live in Switzerland? yes/no'?

'Minor' vs 'Adult in first education': on which date is the child's age judged? The submission date, the first working day, or the start of the tax year? A child who turns 18 around the start date would otherwise be classified differently.

The permit reminder is 'worded by HR', but no text is given. Who provides the final wording and when (before build or configurable later)? Is it shown only at the end, or also elsewhere (e.g. in a confirmation)?

review.summary: All 300+ examples pass. There are no errors, no blocking open questions and no blocker-level dev questions. The package is buildable. Five major dev-refinement questions, five non-blocking open questions, several partly unbacked claims and some internal rule ids in the prose need a product owner decision or cleanup. The tariff logic rests on inferred per-child rows, which D-009 makes a go-live verification gate.

findings.title: Insurance start rule: contract start vs actual first working day
findings.why: If the contract starts on the 1st but the first working day is later (weekend or holiday), the rule moves insurance start to the next month. This gives wrong fund registrations. The fund's link between start date and first working day is also unknown.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (feature.md, major); coverage: F-pension_portal-3a97ab unused; US-03.2
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml whether the rule uses the contractual start date or the actual first working day. Confirm with the fund how mid-month starts are handled.

findings.title: Child per-child result is inferred and internally inconsistent
findings.why: Lonio now computes the tariff itself. The rule expression disagrees with its table in at least two cases, and many rows rest only on D-009, which is a verification decision and not a source. Wrong tariff codes are possible.
findings.evidence: trace_judge rule.child_result; inferred_items; OQ-calculator-coverage; US-07.3 to 07.6
findings.action: Have the domain expert reconcile the expression and the table. Run the inferred rows against the Zurich calculator before go-live, as D-009 requires. Keep this as an explicit release gate.

findings.title: Liechtenstein question order and the reservation under the double taxation agreement
findings.why: Liechtenstein residents who return daily get no tariff code, yet they are still asked about denomination, spouse employment and children. This breaks data minimisation. The 'subject to double taxation agreement' reservation for more than 45 non-return days is not recorded in AC-08.4.3.
findings.action: Decide whether the Liechtenstein questions come first or answers are discarded. Decide whether the reservation is recorded and flagged for HR.

findings.title: Residence country timing
findings.why: The home-address country decides source-tax liability, the canton and the cross-border questions. Movers' current address may differ from the one that applies from the first working day.
findings.action: Decide whether to ask for the address applying at the first working day. Add this to the story.

findings.title: House number required without a source
findings.why: Employees whose address has no house number could not submit.
findings.action: Decide whether the house number is optional or allows an explicit 'no house number'.

findings.title: Fund registration gaps (canton abroad, partnership and separated mapping, divorced and widowed)
findings.why: The fund's canton field is required, but employees abroad have no valid value. The Married mapping for registered partners and separated employees is provisional. Divorced and widowed screens are unseen. Registration could be blocked.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton-abroad; OQ-civil-status-partnership; OQ-spouse-dob-other-status; fact_judge F-pension_portal-b359c3, 6d3630, 39bab1; trace_judge rule.pension_fund_civil_status (Separated not backed)
findings.action: Get the fund's answers and a screenshot for Divorced and Widowed. Record the decisions in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Source tax liability rule is hedged by HR
findings.why: Anna said 'I think so' and added conditions over time. 'Here' is read as Switzerland. This rule gates all the source tax questions.
findings.evidence: OQ-source-tax-rule-confirmation; fact_judge F-hr_transcript-550840 and 5af8d0; trace_judge AC-08.3.1
findings.action: Have HR confirm the decision table in writing, including 'lives here' = Switzerland and that everyone living abroad is subject.

findings.title: Stories include behaviour that no cited fact backs
findings.why: Several claims are untraceable. Examples: the confession, children and spouse-works questions; the fixed step order; the Liechtenstein base-letter handling; the 'no maximum number of children' statement; and the date format and permit reminder purposes. Some cite facts that are not in the cited set.
